result.reason: Both items directly correspond to the content described in the 'Miyayin Veshechar' prose: item 1 is the rejected suggestion about kiddush/havdalah wine (mushba ve'omed me'har sinai), and item 2 is Rava's case of the prior oath to drink wine being overridden by subsequent nezirut — exactly what that section's prose describes.

The passage directly discusses the gemara's give-and-take about why 'veshechar' is needed beyond 'miyayin' — teaching two halakhot including yayin mitzvah — which is precisely what the 'Nezirut as Status' prose describes in its final sentences.

The passage directly explains Rabbi Shimon's use of the verbal analogy (hekesh) between 'shechar' in the nazirite verse and 'shechar' in the Mikdash verse to limit the prohibition to wine only — exactly what the 'Tziruf Concept' prose describes as the gemara's resolution.

The passage quotes the baraita about Rabbi Yehuda's position on pressed figs, honey, and milk causing liability for entering the Temple, which is precisely what the 'Rabbi Yehuda: Shechar' section's prose describes and discusses.

The passage directly states that Rabbi Shimon does not accept the principle of isur chal al isur, which is exactly what the 'No Double Prohibition' section's prose discusses as an alternative explanation for Rabbi Shimon's use of the verse.
The passage is the baraita of Rabbi Shimon about eating neveila on Yom Kippur, which is precisely what the prose under 'Neveila/YK Case' discusses and analyzes.

The passage directly addresses the Rabbis' interpretation of 'mikkol asher ye'aseh migefen ha-yayin' as teaching tziruf (combining of grape-derived prohibitions), which is precisely what the 'Combining Products' section's prose discusses.

The passage discusses Rabbi Shimon's principle of 'kol shehu l'malkot' (smallest quantity suffices for lashes) and the kezayit measure being only for korban — this is the core content introduced in candidate 0's prose, which covers both points together, whereas candidate 1 treats the kezayit-for-korban point as a secondary elaboration after already establishing the kol shehu principle.

The mishna text lists the various formulations that identify one as a nazir Shimshon, which directly matches the 'Identifying Shimshon' section's prose discussing exactly those phrases and the institution of nazir Shimshon.
Both items are the Gemara's explanation of why the mishna needs all its formulations (Shimshon → ben Manoach → ba'al Delilah), which is precisely what the 'Clarification Debate' prose describes.

All five items constitute the mishna and gemara discussing the differences between nazir olam and nazir Shimshon — exactly what the 'Nazir Olam Details' prose section describes, including the michsarei michsara correction and the comparison of their respective leniencies regarding hair-cutting and tumah offerings.

The passage contains exactly the gemara's 'mani matnitin' question and its resolution that the prose of 'Korban Paradox' (index 3) explicitly describes — raising the paradox of who the mishna follows, presenting Rabbi Yehuda's and Rabbi Shimon's positions as a baraita, and resolving that the mishna follows Rabbi Yehuda with the conditional formulation borrowed from the parallel nazir olam case.

All six items constitute the Gemara's discussion of whether Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon's dispute maps onto the Rabbi Yaakov/Rabbi Yosei dispute about bekhor and hatfasah, including the retraction and the full back-and-forth about laHashem, chatat/asham, and matfisan bineder — exactly what the 'Bekhor Transferability' prose describes.

The passage contains Rabbi Yossi's counter-argument that the mitzva to sanctify a bekhor is superfluous since it is already sacred without the act, which is explicitly discussed in the prose of 'Yaakov: Sanctification' (i-lo makdish lei mi lo kadosh) — this is precisely the passage being quoted there.

The passage raises the question of why the 'to the Lord' phrase in the nazirite verse doesn't resolve the Shimshon problem — this is precisely the unresolved question about nazir Shimshon that the 'Shimshon Mystery' section's prose describes as left without a direct answer.

The passage contains the opening of the Shimon HaTzaddik baraita — his declaration that he never ate the asham of a tamei nazir and the introduction of the exceptional man — which directly matches the prose of heading 0 ('Refusing Asham'), not heading 1 which discusses only his question about the hair.

The passage describes the shepherd's story of seeing his reflection, his yetzer hara stirring, and his vow to become a nazir — exactly the content described in the 'Repentance Motivation' prose, which is also the current placement.
